title: Full Workshop: Better Auth — Paola Estefania, Better Auth
talk_summary: A workshop presenting the Agent Auth Protocol: agents get their own identity (private key), discover service capabilities via a directory translated from OpenAPI specs, and request scoped, revocable grants instead of borrowing user credentials. The demo shows an MCP-connected agent requesting read/send email capabilities, user approval via device flow, audit logs per agent, and revocation.

takeaways.technique: Per-agent identity with revocable grants instead of shared credentials
takeaways.what_they_do: Each agent gets its own key/identity and requests scoped capabilities from a server that verifies policy; revoking the agent identity cuts off access without rotating shared secrets.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we need to stop giving credentials our credentials to our agents we need to give them authority

takeaways.technique: Capability directory derived from OpenAPI specs
takeaways.what_they_do: Translate service OpenAPI endpoints into fine-grained capabilities in a directory so agents match intent to specific actions (read vs send vs delete) rather than coarse scopes.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the idea is to use that and convert the two capabilities

takeaways.what_they_do: Hosts (e.g. Claude) get read-only capabilities by default; write actions like sending email require explicit user grant, with constraints like max execution time configurable per capability.
takeaways.evidence_quote: all the hosts like for example clo has reading capabilities by default so then it wouldn't mess up youration with your inbox

takeaways.what_they_do: Because each agent has an identity, every action is logged as 'agent X did Y on behalf of user Z', viewable and filterable by provider/agent.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Which agent did what on behalf of which user

takeaways.technique: Avoid a data-plane proxy; use a directory for intent matching
takeaways.what_they_do: They explicitly reject routing all traffic through a proxy as unscalable and data-heavy; the 'proxy' is only a directory mapping intent to capabilities.
takeaways.evidence_quote: proxy is a really bad idea. It's not scalable because proxy uses data
